patterns.name: AI trade is losing political and market support
patterns.line: Nvidia fell on the Huang probe, US voters backed data centre limits, and money moved to India (ai-2b527a5d8a, ai-31d2e0d061, ai-0087f7f25a). If limits spread, AI capex growth slows and less-exposed markets gain.

patterns.name: AI chips are now a national security fight
patterns.line: The Nvidia probe centres on suspected Chinese intelligence and chip smuggling (ai-2b527a5d8a). Separately, Trump says he could back AI guardrails if the US does not fall behind China (world-4566ea326f).

patterns.name: AI lets firms grow revenue with fewer hires
patterns.line: Indian IT revenue grows 6.1% against 2.3% headcount growth, PhysicsWallah cut staff citing AI, and 52% of Indian CEOs plan some cuts. Entry-level roles are hit first.

patterns.name: Climate policy shifts from preventing to managing overshoot
patterns.line: The world will pass 1.5 °C, so COP31 turns to limiting overshoot and removing CO2 (science-mind-9152cd2db8, india-3568f0f9f6). A super El Niño adds health and food stress (science-mind-14b548b754).

patterns.name: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing
patterns.line: India approved a $1.5B storage scheme with 40% local content, and the IEA sees renewables growth 2.6x faster (climate-energy-b60bb3c081, climate-energy-bebe229e75). Inverter chip imports remain a gap.

money.line: Hyderabad spacetech startup; investors include Rebright Partners, Aranya Holdings, Naandi Ventures, AUM Ventures and Shakti VC.

lead.headline: Nvidia's board opens probe into CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese spy link
lead.hook: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was ==targeted by a foreign intelligence effort==, and its shares fell about 5-6% in pre-market trading on Monday.
points: Huang admitted in a staff memo to an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former Megaspeed executive US officials judged a Chinese intelligence asset. China calls the claim a smear.
Independent directors with outside counsel will run the probe. The board says it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. Huang stays CEO meanwhile.
Megaspeed, a Singapore data centre firm, bought about $4.8B of Nvidia equipment per the NYT, and has faced smuggling claims. It denies violations.
Trump called Huang honorable. Republican lawmakers want a closed-door briefing, and a Congress hearing on November 18 was reported.
Nvidia is down about 22% from its October peak and reports earnings on November 17. __The affair lands one week before results and a Trump-Xi summit.__
signal: If the probe finds data leaked, expect tighter scrutiny of Nvidia's overseas customers and China sales.
Nvidia has no public succession plan, so key-person risk is now a live issue for investors.
lead.editors_read: The company's biggest risk is no longer only export rules but its CEO's credibility with both Washington and Beijing. Huang lobbied for China sales (H200), so any finding of compromise strengthens hawks. Markets already fragile on AI spending have less cushion for this.
lead.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

frontpage.headline: COP31 opens with 1.5 °C overshoot now accepted as inevitable
frontpage.hook: COP31 in Antalya is the first UN climate meeting after the UN Environment Programme said the world will overshoot 1.5 °C under all plausible emissions paths.
points: UNEP's Limiting Overshoot report says hundreds of billions of tonnes of CO2 must be removed this century, via technology or nature such as reforestation, to bring warming back below 1.5 °C.
No country has put clearly quantified CO2 removal targets in its UN climate commitments, says Oxford's Steve Smith.
Scientist Johan Rockström wants COP decisions by majority vote instead of consensus, because a few states can block the rest.
Projected warming this century has fallen from about 4 °C at Paris in 2015 to 2.6-2.8 °C under current policies.
signal: If CO2 removal gets quantified targets, a new industry gets a policy-backed market.
frontpage.editors_read: Governments are admitting the target failed but have no plan for the fix. Whoever first sets measurable removal targets will shape a new market. Consensus rules mean progress will stay slow.
frontpage.evidence_of: Climate policy shifts from preventing to managing overshoot

frontpage.headline: Trump says AI risks are manageable, open to guardrails
frontpage.hook: Trump told CBS's 60 Minutes that AI risks can be managed and he is open to safeguards (summary from limited source text).
points: Crypto Briefing reports he could back guardrails with Democrats, provided rules do not leave the US behind China.
Indian Express notes he has previously favoured letting tech companies police themselves over sweeping government restrictions.
signal: Separately today, Democrats' midterm win and local data centre limits raise pressure for rules (ai-0087f7f25a).
frontpage.editors_read: A shift from his 'let it rip' stance, likely driven by midterm results. The China-race condition suggests any rules will be narrow.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

frontpage.headline: Sheikh Hasina seeks passport, signalling December return to Bangladesh
frontpage.hook: Ousted Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina has requested a new passport and ID card, the clearest sign she will return in December despite a death sentence in absentia.
points: She told Reuters she intends to surrender before a Bangladesh court; aides say the date will be announced after formalities.
A war crimes court sentenced her to death last November over the 2024 crackdown; the UN estimates up to 1,400 people were killed.
Bangladesh's foreign and law ministries are checking whether she can legally apply, and Dhaka wants her extradited from India, which has declined.
She still has support among parts of the population.
signal: Her return could complicate Bangladesh's efforts to stabilise politics and its economy, and strain India-Bangladesh ties if extradition stays contested.
frontpage.editors_read: Surrendering to a court rather than being extradited changes the politics for India, which hosts her. Watch whether Dhaka grants the documents.

frontpage.headline: Parliament's monsoon session stays unprorogued for record 88 days
frontpage.hook: Parliament's monsoon session has stayed unprorogued for 88 days since August 13, passing the 2008 record of 87 days.
points: Not proroguing keeps open a sitting on two days' notice; a fresh session needs at least 14 days.
Speculation centres on a constitutional amendment tied to the Women's Reservation Bill, raising the Lok Sabha from 543 to up to 850 seats through delimitation.
A similar amendment failed to get the required numbers in the Lok Sabha on April 17.
The Constitution sets no time limit, so the delay is not improper.
signal: If the government finds the numbers, it can recall Parliament in two days.
frontpage.editors_read: Keeping the session alive is a tool for speed and surprise. The April failure shows the numbers are the real constraint.

frontpage.headline: Foreign funds pile into Indian stocks as AI trade falters
frontpage.hook: Foreign funds bought close to $5 billion of Indian stocks last week, including $3.6 billion in the first four sessions, as the Nifty 50 rose more than 8%.
points: The Nifty slipped in Sunday's ceremonial Diwali session, its first loss in such trading in nine years.
signal: Separately today, Mint says investors see India as a hedge against AI exposure (ai-31d2e0d061).
frontpage.editors_read: India is gaining because it lacks AI stocks, which hurt it earlier. The flow could reverse if AI sentiment recovers.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI trade is losing political and market support

frontpage.headline: Timed pink noise during sleep boosted brain-fluid flow in a study
frontpage.hook: Short bursts of pink noise timed to sleep slow-wave peaks raised cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow versus no-noise control periods, in a Science Translational Medicine study.
points: The glymphatic system flushes brain waste with CSF during sleep; ageing and poor sleep disrupt it.
Researchers used an algorithm to time noise to slow-wave peaks while participants slept in an MRI machine.
Timing matters: playing pink noise all night would not give the same effect, says the lead author.
The team does not know why it works, and has not shown that waste is actually cleared; animal follow-ups are planned.
signal: If validated, it is a non-invasive therapy for older people and those with sleep disorders, but this is early evidence.
frontpage.evidence_of: Science is finding non-drug ways to treat the brain

frontpage.headline: DeepSeek's Harness agent framework hits 1.54 million daily users
frontpage.hook: DeepSeek says its Harness AI agent framework reached 1.54 million daily active users less than three months after launch, consuming about 92 trillion tokens a day.
points: A harness is the software that turns a language model into an agent that carries out tasks. OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude Code are built on theirs.
Harness launched August 13, with a desktop app on September 29. It has about 35,000 third-party plug-ins; around 60% of active users have built or installed one.
DeepSeek plans a plug-in marketplace and developer grants, and set up its first product division last month.
signal: DeepSeek is moving from models toward monetising products, taking the agent contest to US rivals.
frontpage.evidence_of: Model makers are competing on agent software

frontpage.headline: India's outsourcing industry grows revenue faster than headcount
frontpage.hook: Nasscom projects FY2026 tech revenue of $315 billion, up 6.1%, while employment grows only 2.3%, adding about 135,000 workers to 5.95 million.
points: AI shortens routine coding, testing and support work: a project needing 20 engineers might need 15. Hourly billing makes this hurt revenue, so firms push for outcome-based pricing.
The top five IT firms added 16,055 net staff in H1 FY2027 versus 3,097 a year earlier, but hiring is shifting to experienced cloud, cybersecurity and data engineers.
The ILO says AI has slowed recruitment of younger workers rather than causing mass layoffs.
India had 2,117 global capability centres in FY2026 employing about 2.36 million and earning $98.4B, but they hire selectively.
The Philippines cut its 2028 targets to $43.3-50.5B revenue and 1.85-2.14 million workers.
signal: Fewer entry-level jobs is the real risk, since firms need juniors to become future seniors.
frontpage.editors_read: Firms keep margins but cut the entry rung that trains talent. Expect pricing to move from hours to outcomes.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI lets firms grow revenue with fewer hires

stories.headline: Opinion: anti-AI populism will define US politics
stories.hook: Local restrictions on data centres passed in more than 30 localities across nine states, and 41% of planned capacity sits in states with governors-elect backing moratoriums, writes Garrison Lovely.
points: NBC exit polls: 23% of voters called AI and data centres crucial, and Democrats won them 67% to 30%.
On which party is better on AI, 30% said Democrats, 27% Republicans, 43% neither.
More than 130 federal and gubernatorial races mentioned tech accountability or AI in ads.
Musk's near-$500M spending failed: Republicans lost all five Senate races he spent most on.
Lovely, author of a book arguing for stopping AGI development, urges subpoena-backed hearings and worker-protection laws. This is opinion.
signal: If data centre limits spread, AI capex plans face real local constraints.
stories.evidence_of: AI trade is losing political and market support

stories.headline: India's MeitY releases three state-backed AI models
stories.hook: MeitY, through the IndiaAI Mission, unveiled EKA-1, a 26.3-billion-parameter model supporting all 22 scheduled languages, plus Dhīr 5B and 2B, open-source models that run offline.
points: EKA-1, from Soket Labs, trained on 7.5 trillion tokens with a 64K-token context window and a mixture-of-experts design (only part of the model runs per query).
Dhīr models, from ZenteiQ, are open under Apache 2.0 on AIKosh and Hugging Face. The 2B runs in 1.5-2GB of RAM, the article says.
Both firms used subsidised compute under the ₹10,372-crore mission, including Google Cloud TPUs and C-DAC clusters.
Their Indic-script tokenizers reduce the token cost that Western models impose on Indian languages, the article says, claiming up to 75% lower latency.
signal: Performance claims are the vendors' own; independent benchmarks are needed. Open on-device models could cut API costs for Indian language apps.
stories.evidence_of: Countries are funding sovereign AI models

stories.headline: What the global AI rout means for India
stories.hook: After the Nasdaq fell 5.5% on 5 November, foreign investors bought $1.6 billion of Indian shares, their largest one-day purchase in nearly six years.
points: AI-linked firms are about 16% of MSCI India versus 70-80% in Taiwan and Korea (Goldman). On 6 November the Kospi fell 6% while the Nifty rose about 2%.
India's own 42 'AI Enablers' fell up to 8%; they had risen about 58% since January and trade at an 85% premium to the market.
India has about 1.5GW of data centre capacity against about 50GW in the US. Indian-only users make under 13% of operational capacity and about 80% of subsidised GPUs reportedly sit unused (Rhodium).
Clients want the same IT work 25-30% cheaper (Persistent). AI is about 8% of Infosys revenue, so it must grow 23-35% a year to offset 2-3% annual declines in traditional work.
India's model builders are small: seven of Goldman's 84 leading private AI firms, worth about $2B of $55B.
signal: India is a hedge on the way down but not insulated: equipment, IT services and data centre demand all depend on foreign AI spending.
stories.evidence_of: AI trade is losing political and market support

also.line: Cushman & Wakefield projects India's office-using workforce rising from about 38 million in 2025 to 48 million by 2030, adding roughly 1.8 million a year despite AI.

stories.headline: China pushes specialised industrial AI beyond language models
stories.hook: A Tsinghua professor says language models struggle with structured industrial data, and his team's LimiX model, trained only on synthetic data, cut deployment cost and time by about 90%.
points: Cui Peng says LLMs are hard to use for factory sensor and financial records; LimiX is a 'large data model' built with Wenzhun Intelligence.
He claims accuracy improved by more than 15% on average, including in fusion research.
Beijing's 'AI plus' plan targets over 70% penetration of AI agents and devices by 2027.
Huawei says local governments in Zhejiang and Guangdong coordinate AI adoption by industry.
signal: Results are the researchers' claims. China is competing on deployment through infrastructure, not only on model strength.
stories.evidence_of: China is pushing AI into industry

also.line: Physicists in Poland, Zurich and France observed a supersolid (crystal-like order with frictionless flow) in light-matter particles at room temperature, avoiding extreme cooling; applications like optical computing remain speculative.

stories.headline: Ex-IAF chief calls HAL's rejection of indigenous radar a 'bad decision'
stories.hook: Former Air Chief Marshal Bhadauria says HAL erred by buying more Israeli EL/M-2052 radars for the Tejas Mk1A instead of DRDO's Uttam radar.
points: He says flight-test data shows Uttam gives more range than the radar being integrated, and is ready for induction.
He suggests HAL chose foreign hardware as it is easier to certify and HAL already co-produces the Israeli radar.
Mk2 delay is partly due to undercarriage problems; he says HAL project management has been 'disastrous' and defence PSUs spend too little on R&D.
HAL's AMCA bid failed because one partner missed technical criteria; private bids are now submitted.
signal: Choices like this decide whether indigenous components get production volume.
stories.evidence_of: India is shifting defence development toward private industry

stories.headline: Zipline raises $1.5B at $21.5B valuation for drone delivery
stories.hook: Zipline raised $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion post-money valuation led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management and Layer Global.
points: It signed a multi-year Walmart deal for 300 additional delivery sites; Uber targets one million deliveries a day through Zipline by 2029.
It completed over one million deliveries in Dallas-Fort Worth this year; median October delivery took 19 minutes versus over 30 for traditional delivery.
The funds go to US manufacturing, hiring and a nationwide network.
signal: Large retail contracts suggest drone delivery is moving past pilots, though figures are company-reported.
stories.evidence_of: Capital is flowing to hard-tech logistics

stories.headline: India's renewable boom set to be faster than ever, IEA says
stories.hook: India's renewable capacity growth in 2025-2031 is likely to be 2.6 times the pace of the prior six years, and India will supply 9% of global additions.
points: India moved from fourth to third in installed renewable capacity and may become second behind China within five years.
India has 233 GW of solar module capacity, but cells, wafers and polysilicon are almost all imported.
In China, 90% of major solar makers lose money, over 70 firms have gone bankrupt since 2024, and solar additions fell 55% in nine months.
The government approved ₹14,500 crore for grid storage; India needs about 411 GWh by March 2032.
signal: Grid equipment and storage makers may benefit more than generators if transmission is the bottleneck.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

stories.headline: India approves $1.5B scheme for 92 GWh of grid storage
stories.hook: India's cabinet approved a ₹14,500 crore ($1.5B) scheme to build 92 GWh of grid storage over five years, expected to draw about $10B in investment.
points: The plan: 60 GWh pumped hydro, 30 GWh batteries, 2 GWh emerging technologies; about 170% of existing grid storage.
Battery projects need 40% domestic content.
India needs about 411 GWh by 2031-32, but only about 9.1 GWh of battery storage worked by September 2026, under 4% of that.
Without storage, surplus solar goes unused and coal covers evening demand.
signal: Domestic content rules favour local battery assemblers but could raise costs if cell supply stays imported.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

stories.headline: India has commissioned 8,000 tonnes a year of green hydrogen capacity
stories.hook: India had commissioned about 8,000 tonnes of annual green hydrogen capacity by February 2026, against a 2030 target of at least 5 million tonnes.
points: Green hydrogen is made by splitting water with renewable electricity. The mission has a ₹19,744 crore outlay.
Incentives went to 15 firms for 3,000 MW of electrolyser manufacturing and to production capacity of 8.62 lakh tonnes a year.
Offtake commitments exceed 5.5 lakh tonnes a year by October 2026.
Pilots include five steel projects, 70 hydrogen vehicles, and a hydrogen train inaugurated July 17, 2026.
signal: The gap between 8,000 tonnes and 5 million tonnes depends on cheap renewable power and firm buyers.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

stories.headline: Solar inverter localisation in India faces semiconductor hurdles
stories.hook: Industry executives say India's solar inverter makers depend on imported power electronics, especially semiconductors, which complicates proposed domestic-content rules under an ALMM list for inverters.
points: ALMM is the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers.
Executives warn stricter domestic content requirements could raise costs.
signal: Local-content rules can raise project costs if chip supply stays imported.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

also.line: Residential rooftop solar under PM Surya Ghar passed 19 GW in October 2026 (19,189 MW across 65.26 lakh households), led by Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat.

stories.headline: COP31 opens in Turkey; India plans to speak for the Global South
stories.hook: COP31 runs 9-20 November in Antalya, with Turkey as host and Australia leading negotiations; India's minister Bhupender Yadav joins in the second week.
points: India will press for climate justice, climate finance and developed-country technology transfer, and opposes new top-down emission targets.
Copernicus says 2026 is virtually certain to exceed 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels, in one of the worst El Niño years on record.
Turkey's voluntary targets include 35% global electrification and 25% lower building energy intensity by 2035.
signal: Expect India to resist any overshoot text that imposes uniform cuts.
stories.evidence_of: Climate policy shifts from preventing to managing overshoot

stories.headline: Delhi tries 'green' fireworks at Diwali
stories.hook: India's top court allowed only greener fireworks this weekend, citing air quality, but activists call it greenwash (summary from limited source text).
points: Green fireworks may emit less smoke in controlled tests, but scientists and doctors doubt the real-world difference.
signal: Real air quality outcomes will test the ruling.

stories.headline: Signing FTAs is not enough to lift India's exports
stories.hook: Only an estimated 20-30% of India's eligible exports use FTA preferences, versus 60-70% in developed markets, per Bank of America.
points: Exporters face proof-of-origin rules, certification and carbon reporting; the EU deal is awaiting implementation early next year.
Many components are imported from China, making Indian origin hard to prove.
MSMEs bear upfront costs for testing and audits before any order; they account for 45% of exports.
Deficits with South Korea and Japan tripled after older pacts; those deals are under review.
signal: Gains will go first to firms with compliance systems unless smaller firms get help.
stories.evidence_of: Trade deals need compliance capacity to pay off

stories.headline: Gen Z protests are spreading across the world
stories.hook: Researchers have documented at least 25 protests worldwide in which Gen Z (roughly ages 14-29) played a role.
points: Serbia's students ousted Vučić's party after 14 years in elections; Lula won in Brazil with youth mobilisation online.
Organisers use TikTok, X, Discord and VPNs to coordinate and bypass internet shutdowns.
India's Cockroach movement forced the education minister to resign; authorities detained thousands and shut the internet in October.
Youth protests often meet harsher repression: Morocco charged over 2,000 people.
signal: Breakdown of the social contract is the shared cause, per analysts; repression raises the cost of protest.
stories.evidence_of: Young people are driving political change

stories.headline: RBI reportedly queries banks' valuation of bond forward trades
stories.hook: The RBI has told some lenders to value bond forward contracts using Level 3 inputs, covering billions of dollars across the industry, people familiar say (summary from limited source text).
points: The instruction came in recent in-person audits.
signal: Level 3 valuations rely on unobservable inputs, which can cause bigger swings in reported profits.

also.line: An RBA official says surging AI-related investment will add to demand and put near-term pressure on inflation in Australia.

stories.headline: The super El Niño is also a health shock
stories.hook: The University of Chicago's Climate Impact Lab projects 451,000 extra heat-related deaths from the 2026-27 El Niño, mainly in low- and middle-income countries.
points: Eastern Pacific temperatures already exceed the four other very strong El Niños of the past 50 years.
The 1982-83 and 1997-98 events cost $4.1 trillion and $5.7 trillion in global income.
It arrives amid wars and fertiliser shortages, raising food-price and malnutrition risks.
Food shortages may increase wild meat reliance, raising disease risk.
signal: Local food prices, not global ones, decide how bad this gets.
stories.evidence_of: Climate policy shifts from preventing to managing overshoot

stories.headline: New CAR-T therapy cleared a childhood brain tumour in every mouse tested
stories.hook: UCSF's B-SYNC CAR-T cells completely eliminated diffuse midline glioma, a childhood cancer almost always fatal within a year, in two mouse models.
points: The cells switch on only when they sense brevican, a brain protein, so they stay inactive elsewhere.
Treated mice rejected new cancer cells about seven weeks later, and cells stayed active beyond 70 days.
Conventional CAR-T could not control the tumours.
Human trials could begin as early as April 2027.
signal: Mouse results often fail in humans; the trial will test safety first.
stories.evidence_of: Science is finding new ways to treat hard cancers

stories.headline: Stickier ocean 'snow' carries six times more carbon to the deep
stories.hook: Highly viscous marine snow can carry more than six times as much carbon to the deep ocean as thinner particles, researchers report in Science.
points: Marine snow removes over 10 gigatons of carbon a year from surface waters, but only about 2 gigatons reach depths where it stays for centuries.
Bacteria colonise less viscous outer areas and struggle to break down stickier cores.
New 3D imaging let researchers watch bacteria interact with the particles for the first time.
signal: Better carbon-cycle models may need viscosity included.
stories.evidence_of: Science is finding new ways ocean carbon storage works

stories.headline: MakeMyTrip's India arm gets Sebi nod for IPO
stories.hook: MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd received Sebi's final observations on November 6 for an IPO, after filing confidentially in July.
points: The IPO will be a sale of existing shares by parent MakeMyTrip and its subsidiary ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore), so the parent keeps control.
Proceeds go to the parent for growth, acquisitions and repurchases of securities.
MakeMyTrip posted a $1.8M Q2 FY27 profit versus a $5.7M loss a year earlier, on revenue of $235.2M, up 11.2%.
signal: Listing gives MMT India stock to use for hiring.

stories.headline: PhysicsWallah cuts staff citing AI and earmarks under $20M for M&A
stories.hook: PhysicsWallah's headcount, about 19,100, fell sequentially in Q2 FY27, partly due to AI efficiencies, and management says AI writes about 90% of its code.
points: Employee expenses fell 2.3% year-on-year excluding ESOP costs.
Q2 revenue was ₹1,242 crore (up 18%) and net profit ₹142 crore, up from ₹70 crore.
The offline business lost ₹108 crore at EBITDA level in H1 FY27, versus ₹120 crore a year earlier; it runs 370 centres, including 167 Vidyapeeth.
It is in advanced talks with a couple of online education firms, with under $20M earmarked; M&A will add under 5% to FY27 growth.
signal: A listed Indian startup is openly linking AI to a smaller workforce.
stories.evidence_of: AI lets firms grow revenue with fewer hires

also.line: Inc42 says key new-age tech stocks in ecommerce, fintech and logistics improved profitability and topline in Q2 FY27 despite a muted start to the festive season.

stories.headline: 52% of Indian CEOs plan some AI-linked job cuts, yet 92% expect headcount to grow
stories.hook: KPMG's survey of 125 Indian CEOs finds 52% plan workforce cuts in some areas, up from 50% in 2025, while 92% expect total headcount to grow over three years.
points: 78% rank AI a top investment priority, against 79% globally.
86% are reviewing skills needed for entry-level jobs, versus 76% globally.
62% will put 11-20% of budgets into AI, and 70% expect returns in one to three years.
Top barriers are ethics (64%) and inconsistent regional AI regulation (53%).
signal: Work is being restructured rather than cut overall; entry-level roles are the ones being redefined.
stories.evidence_of: AI lets firms grow revenue with fewer hires

opportunities.name: Top Business Schools Present: Application Tips (Virtual)
opportunities.summary: Admissions teams from ten MBA programmes (Booth, Harvard, Stanford, Wharton, Kellogg, Columbia and others) share application tips. Online.
